newsitem.title: INDIA: Two Mexicans believed abducted were sightseeing.
newsitem.headline: Two Mexicans believed abducted were sightseeing.

text.p: Two Mexican engineers believed to have been kidnapped in northern India over the weekend had gone sightseeing without informing their employer, police said on Monday.

"Initially, the manager (of the plant) had lodged a complaint with the police that the engineers had been kidnapped. But on investigation it was found that they had gone on their own to Agra," Punjab state police chief Puran Chand Dogra said.
The city of Agra is home to the famed Taj Mahal.

The United News of India news agency earlier said engineers Eduardo Moral and Sergo Orlix Sanchez, on an assignment at a brewery in Punjab, had been kidnapped on Saturday on their way from the factory to their hotel in Ludhiana city.
At least 20,000 people were killed during a Sikh separatist revolt in the 1980s which rocked Punjab. The violence died down after local elections in 1992.
Dogra said: "The engineers are expected back at the plant on Monday evening. They had checked out of their hotel in Ludhiana and had taken away all their documents."

"So there are no cases made of kidnapping till they return," he said. "Before they left the plant, the engineers told the workers that they were going away for sightseeing to Agra and may come back on Monday evening."
A spokesman at the Mexican embassy in New Delhi earlier said he had no information about Moral and Sanchez.
